Book Description & Praise

内容简介与推荐语

“This book gets something most leadership guides miss: you can’t optimize your way out of chaos with frameworks alone. Juan Pablo and James show how psychological safety, clear direction, and disciplined execution work together, and why getting that wrong costs teams more than they realize.”
— Dr. Nicole Forsgren, Senior Director of Developer Intelligence at Google and coauthor of Accelerate

“这本书抓住了大多数领导力指南忽略的一点：你不可能只靠框架就把混乱优化掉。Juan Pablo 和 James 展示了心理安全感、清晰方向与纪律化执行如何协同作用，以及把这三者搞砸会让团队付出多大的代价。”
— Dr. Nicole Forsgren，Google 开发者智能高级总监，《Accelerate》合著者

Whether they’re building a startup or scaling an established org, engineering leaders know the real job is keeping chaos under control. In a world of shifting priorities, scarce resources, and rapid change, leadership means embracing the unknown, managing moving targets, and creating clarity where there’s none. Sometimes, you’re building the plane as you’re flying it—writing the roadmap as you go, designing processes in real time.

无论是在创业公司，还是在扩张中的成熟组织，工程领导者都清楚：真正的工作是把混乱控制住。在优先级不断变化、资源稀缺、快速迭代的世界里，领导力意味着拥抱未知、管理移动靶心，并在一片混沌中创造出清晰。有时候，你就是一边飞一边造飞机——边走边写路线图，实时设计流程。

Engineering Leadership: The Hard Parts cuts through the noise, offering a guide for tackling these gritty, real-world challenges. Current and future leaders, this is your toolkit. It’s packed with principles, techniques, and mental models for thriving in uncertainty.

《工程领导力：硬功夫》拨开噪音，为应对这些粗糙而真实的挑战提供了一份指南。现任与未来的领导者们，这就是你的工具箱。里面装满了在不确定中茁壮成长所需的原则、技巧与心智模型。

  • Navigate the full scope: Step into engineering leadership’s complex, multifaceted role

    把握全貌：走进工程领导这一复杂、多面的角色

  • Build high-impact teams: Master advanced techniques to grow and lead your technical talent

    打造高影响力团队：掌握进阶技巧，培养并带领你的技术人才

  • Align and execute: Connect strategy to business outcomes, scale effectively, and balance innovation with precision

    对齐与执行：把战略连到业务结果，有效扩张，在创新与精准之间取得平衡

  • Lead with resilience: Adapt quickly and drive continuous improvement

    韧性领导：快速适应，推动持续改进

  • Accelerate your career: Develop your leadership edge and unlock new growth

    加速职业发展：锤炼你的领导力优势，解锁新的成长空间

Juan Pablo Buriticá is CTO at Convergint and has built engineering teams at Stripe and Splice. Known for scaling distributed teams and cultivating technical excellence, he’s also helped grow Latin America’s tech community through events and by founding a major Spanish-JavaScript collective.

Juan Pablo Buriticá 现任 Convergint CTO，曾在 Stripe 和 Splice 搭建工程团队。他以扩张分布式团队、培育技术卓越文化而闻名；同时他还通过举办活动、创立大型西班牙语 JavaScript 社区，助力拉美科技圈成长。

James Turnbull is a product and engineering leader with experience across startups and enterprise tech. He has held roles at Smartrr, Kickstarter, Venmo, Sotheby’s, and Microsoft. A former chair of the O’Reilly Velocity Conference series, he also advises startups and has authored 11 technical books.

James Turnbull 是一位产品与工程领导者，在创业公司与大型企业科技领域均有经验。他曾任职于 Smartrr、Kickstarter、Venmo、Sotheby’s 和 Microsoft。他曾任 O’Reilly Velocity 大会系列主席，同时为创业公司提供咨询，并著有 11 本技术书籍。

Preface

序言

When we—Juan Pablo and James—first met, it was in a breakfast group for startup engineering leaders. We both worked at startups with varying levels of chaos and dysfunction. What was interesting to both of us were the similarities between our experiences. Despite different organizations, people, and products, we saw that when rapid change and chaotic situations occurred (startup life™), people and organizations responded similarly—with the same, less-than-optimal outcomes. Our wider breakfast group also shared similar experiences. (The group was part networking and part support system.) Fast-forward 10+ years, and we’ve both been in big and small organizations where we’ve had to deal with the same chaos and dysfunction. In recent years, we’ve worked together on several projects and been able to compare notes in greater depth. What continued to intrigue us was that these recurring patterns persisted.

我们俩——Juan Pablo 和 James——最初是在一个创业公司工程负责人早餐会上认识的。当时我们都在不同的创业公司，各自面对不同程度的混乱与功能失调。让我们都觉得有意思的，是彼此经历之间的相似之处。尽管组织、人员、产品都不同，但我们发现：当快速变化和混乱局面来临时（也就是所谓的“创业生活™”），人和组织的反应惊人地相似——结果同样地差强人意。我们那个更大的早餐小组也分享着类似经历（这个小组一半是人脉，一半是互助）。一晃十几年过去，我们都在大大小小的组织里继续面对同样的混乱与失调。最近几年，我们一起做了几个项目，得以更深入地交换心得。让我们一直好奇的是：那些反复出现的模式，居然一直都在。

Over those years, we’ve developed approaches, strategies, and techniques to handle chaotic environments and achieve better outcomes for our teams and organizations. We don’t approach these problems identically, and we each have our spheres of strengths and domains that interest us. Hence, a regular part of our interactions involved comparing notes on areas where we were weaker.

这些年里，我们摸索出了一套应对混乱环境、为团队和组织取得更好结果的方法、策略与技巧。我们俩处理问题的方式并不相同，各自有擅长的领域和感兴趣的方向。因此，我们日常交流中很重要的一部分，就是在各自不擅长的领域互相交换心得。

In addition, several significant chaotic events have stressed leaders and their teams in recent years—for example, dealing with COVID-19 or managing teams of engineers living in war zones and facing political and environmental upheaval. Those experiences, along with anecdotes we heard from our peers, suggested that dealing with chaos was an industry-wide challenge for engineering leaders. We decided to codify our developed approaches and techniques, first as a training course and now as a book.

此外，近年来多起重大的混乱事件给领导者及其团队带来了巨大压力——例如应对新冠疫情，或是管理身处战区、面对政治与环境剧变的工程师团队。这些经历，加上我们从同行那里听到的各种故事，都表明：应对混乱是工程领导者全行业共同的挑战。于是我们决定把自己摸索出的方法和技巧整理成文，先做成一门培训课程，现在变成了这本书。

While the ideas we share in this book may help you survive engineering leadership in chaotic organizations and times, we don’t believe they are a cure-all. Still, we hope they will support you on your leadership journey. This book contains hard-won knowledge gathered through some tough professional challenges that we’d prefer you not to face, or it might at least help lessen the impact of those experiences you cannot avoid.

我们希望这本书里分享的思路，能帮你在混乱的组织和时代中撑过工程领导力这一关，但我们并不认为它是万灵药。尽管如此，我们仍希望它能在你的领导之路上给你支持。这本书里的知识来之不易，是我们经历过若干段痛苦的职业考验后换来的——我们宁愿你不必经历这些考验；即便有些考验你躲不过，也希望这本书能帮你减轻它们的冲击。

— 原书第 15 页 —

Who Should Read This Book

谁应该读这本书

As an engineering leader, you’re responsible for your team’s success and the delivery of complex technical projects. This is challenging even under the best circumstances, but it can feel downright impossible within a chaotic environment.

作为工程领导者，你要为团队的成功和复杂技术项目的交付负责。即便在最好的情况下，这也很有挑战；而在一个混乱的环境里，这简直让人觉得根本做不到。

You may be a new engineering manager, suddenly responsible for a team and a codebase that you’re still learning to navigate. You’re trying to figure out how to balance your team’s needs with the business’s demands, all while establishing your own leadership style and earning the trust of your reports.

你可能是一位新上任的工程经理，突然要带一支团队、守一套你自己都还在摸索的代码库。你正努力搞清楚如何在团队需求和业务诉求之间找平衡，同时还要建立自己的领导风格、赢得下属的信任。

Or perhaps you’re a seasoned director or vice president, but you’ve landed in an organization that’s growing faster than its processes and structure can keep up. You’re working long hours to keep things on track, but it feels like you’re always firefighting and never have time for strategic planning or team development.

又或者，你已经是一位经验丰富的总监或 VP，却掉进了一家组织——它的增长速度远远超过了流程和结构能跟上的节奏。你每天加班加点想让事情上轨道，却感觉自己永远在救火，根本没时间做战略规划或团队发展。

You might be a technical leader—a staff engineer or architect—trying to lead without formal authority. You see the technical challenges and risks that must be addressed, but need help gaining buy-in and alignment from organizational stakeholders.

你也可能是一位技术领导者——资深工程师或架构师——在没有正式职权的情况下想推动事情。你看到了必须解决的技术挑战和风险，却需要有人帮你获得组织内利益相关方的认同与对齐。

Regardless of your specific role or context, leading in a chaotic environment is draining. You likely juggle multiple roles and navigate endless obstacles and surprises. It can be frustrating, stressful, and demoralizing.

无论你的具体角色和处境如何，在混乱环境中带队都是极其消耗精力的。你很可能身兼数职，在无穷无尽的障碍和意外中穿行。这过程可能令人沮丧、压力山大、士气低落。

But here’s the thing: as hard as it is, your leadership matters now more than ever. In the face of chaos and uncertainty, your team needs someone to provide direction, clarity, and support. They need someone to advocate for them and clear the path for their work. They need someone to create a pocket of sanity and stability where they can focus and do their best work.

但关键在于：尽管很难，你的领导力此刻比以往任何时候都更重要。面对混乱与不确定性，你的团队需要有人给出方向、理清思路、提供支持。他们需要有人替他们发声、为他们扫清工作障碍。他们需要有人在混乱中造出一小块清醒与稳定的空间，让他们能专注、能发挥出最好的水平。

That someone is you. You have the opportunity and responsibility to be the leader that your team needs. It won’t be easy, but it is possible—and this book is here to help. By sharing our experiences and lessons, we aim to equip you with the mindsets and techniques necessary to navigate and succeed as a leader under challenging circumstances.

那个人就是你。你有机会、也有责任成为你的团队所需要的那种领导者。这不容易，但完全做得到——而这本书就是来帮你的。通过分享我们的经验和教训，我们希望让你具备在艰难处境中穿迷雾、打胜仗所需的心态和技巧。

Why You Should Read This Book

为什么你应该读这本书

When it comes to books on leadership and management, there is no shortage of options. Walk into any bookstore or browse online, and you’ll find shelves upon shelves of titles promising to make you a better leader. Many of these books are excellent—we’ve read lots of them and have learned a great deal from their insights and advice.

说到领导力和管理类书籍，选择一点也不稀缺。走进任何一家书店或在网上浏览，你都会看到一排排书向你承诺：读了它，你就能成为更好的领导者。这些书中很多都非常优秀——我们读过不少，也从它们的洞见和建议中学到很多。

However, we’ve also found that much of this advice implicitly assumes that you operate in a relatively stable and functional environment. The case studies and examples often feature organizations with clear structures, well-defined processes, and ample resources to invest in new initiatives and professional development.

然而我们也发现，这些建议大多隐含一个前提：你所在的环境相对稳定、运转良好。书里的案例和例子，往往是那些结构清晰、流程明确、资源充裕——可以大把投入新项目和员工发展的组织。

— 原书第 16 页 —

But what if that’s not your reality? What if you’re trying to lead in an organization that’s more chaotic than calm—where roles and responsibilities are unclear, priorities change by the day, and you’re lucky to get through a meeting without being pulled into the latest fire drill?

但如果那不是你的现实呢？如果你试图带领的组织更多是混乱而非平静呢——角色和职责模糊，优先级一天一变，你能开完一场会不被拉去救最新一场火就算走运？

In these situations, much of the standard leadership advice falls flat. It’s not that it’s bad advice—it’s just not feasible to implement when you’re barely keeping your head above water. Telling a leader in a chaotic environment to “just” implement a new process or “just” carve out time for strategic planning is like telling a drowning person to “just” swim to shore. It’s not helpful when you’re consumed by treading water.

在这种处境下，大多数标准的领导力建议都会落空。倒不是那些建议不好——而是当你 barely 能把头露出水面时，根本没条件去落地。告诉一个身处混乱环境的领导者“只要”推行一个新流程、或“只要”挤出时间做战略规划，就像告诉一个快淹死的人“只要”游到岸边就行。当你全部精力都用来踩水时，这种话毫无帮助。

That’s where this book comes in. We’ve both been in the thick of chaotic organizations and had to figure out how to lead and ship products despite the disorder. We’ve had to adapt the best practices and principles of engineering leadership to fit the constraints and challenges of our environments.

这正是这本书的用武之地。我们俩都曾深陷混乱的组织之中，必须在无序中搞清楚怎么带团队、怎么交付产品。我们不得不把工程领导力的最佳实践和原则加以改造，去适应我们所处环境的种种约束和挑战。

In this book, we want to share what we’ve learned. We offer a framework for making sense of the chaos and finding your footing as a leader. We provide concrete strategies and techniques for common challenges like clarifying priorities, making decisions with limited information, communicating effectively, and caring for your team and yourself.

在这本书里，我们想把学到的东西分享出来。我们提供了一个框架，帮你在混乱中理出头绪、站稳脚跟。针对那些常见挑战——厘清优先级、在信息有限时做决策、有效沟通、照顾好你的团队和你自己——我们给出具体的策略和技巧。

Importantly, our advice is grounded in the realities of leading in less-than-ideal circumstances. We know you need more time, resources, and authority. We know you’re dealing with ambiguity, politics, and competing demands. Our goal is to equip you with tools and mental models that you can adapt and apply in your unique context.

重要的是，我们的建议扎根于在不理想处境中带队的真实情况。我们知道你缺时间、缺资源、缺职权。我们知道你要面对模糊地带、办公室政治和相互冲突的诉求。我们的目标，是给你一套工具和心智模型，让你能根据自己独特的处境去调整和运用。

If you’re looking for a playbook to transform your organization into a perfectly oiled machine, this isn’t it. But if you’re looking for practical guidance on navigating the messy, human realities of leading in times of uncertainty and change, keep reading.

如果你想要的是一本把组织改造成完美润滑机器的操作手册，那这本书不是。但如果你想要的是务实的指导——帮你在不确定和变革的时代，穿行于那些 messy、充满人性的带队现实——那就继续读下去。

In the book, we’ll also walk you through the skills and techniques you’ll need to be successful in leading through chaos. The book is divided into two halves. The first part focuses on understanding your role, navigating chaos, setting directions and strategy, and building your team’s resilience and skills:

在书中，我们还会带你走一遍在混乱中带队所需的技能和技巧。全书分为上下两部分。上半部分聚焦于理解你的角色、穿越混乱、设定方向与战略，以及打造团队的韧性与能力：

  • Chapter 1: Understanding what chaos and its symptoms look like

    第 1 章：理解混乱及其症状长什么样

  • Chapter 2: Understanding your role and creating leadership foundations

    第 2 章：理解你的角色，打下领导力基础

  • Chapter 3: Navigating your role in chaotic environments and learning how to deal with the challenges that chaotic environments throw at you

    第 3 章：在混乱环境中找准自己的角色，学会应对混乱抛给你的各种挑战

— 原书第 17 页 —

  • Chapter 4: Building your team into people who thrive in chaos

    第 4 章：把你的团队打造成能在混乱中茁壮成长的人

  • Chapter 5: Setting direction for your team

    第 5 章：为你的团队设定方向

The second half of the book focuses on techniques that you can use to deliver software and set your team up for technical success:

下半部分则聚焦于你可以用来交付软件、为团队铺好技术成功之路的技巧：

  • Chapter 6: Shipping products and code in chaotic environments

    第 6 章：在混乱环境中交付产品与代码

  • Chapter 7: Budgeting, costs, and dealing with vendors

    第 7 章：预算、成本与供应商管理

  • Chapter 8: Developing technical strategy and principles that are resilient to chaos

    第 8 章：制定能抵御混乱的技术战略与原则

  • Chapter 9: Building collaboration and making technical decisions in a chaotic world

    第 9 章：在混乱世界中建立协作、做出技术决策

  • Chapter 10: Metrics that help your team navigate the chaos

    第 10 章：帮你的团队穿越混乱的度量指标

  • Chapter 11: Wrapping it all up—bringing together the principles and techniques we’ve shared

    第 11 章：收尾——把我们分享的原则和技巧融会贯通

We believe that chaos doesn’t have to be a barrier to effective leadership—it can be an opportunity. By embracing the uncertainty and learning to lead through it, you can emerge as a more resilient, adaptable, and confident leader. And in turn, you can help your team and your organization find stability and success on the other side.

我们相信，混乱未必是有效领导力的障碍——它也可以是机会。拥抱不确定性、学会在其中带队，你就能蜕变成一个更有韧性、更灵活、更自信的领导者。反过来，你也能帮助你的团队和组织，在混乱的另一端找到稳定与成功。
